chapter_title: Concerning Four Hunters of Light and Four of Darkn
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Hunters

---

**¶2**

The first seeking power is the Primordial Divine Good that was sent forth from the Infinite. It cast itself down into the five repositories of falsity from evil; it confronted and bound the active opposition of hell [GAP-1] — its drawing influence also [GAP-2] extended over all who dwell in states of falsity [GAP-3]. Its containing doctrine is the four derivative goods that clothe its essential being as an outward form. The pervading state of falsity is the realm of spiritual darkness [GAP-4]; its means of reaching into that realm is [GAP-5] the whole of its proceeding powers.

---

**¶3**

The second seeking power is the Mediating Divine Principle. This one — by the manifest likeness of divine truth which it revealed to the lowest spiritual states — drew forth all wisdom that is latent within all created things, insofar as wisdom is implanted in them. Its drawing influence is its manifest likeness of divine truth, [GAP-6] pervading the whole field of spiritual existence and bringing it into subjection to that likeness [GAP-7]. Its containing doctrine is the doctrine of luminous truth. [GAP-8: REVIEW — The pervading state] is the whole of spiritual existence [GAP-9] — all that was drawn by its influence [GAP-10] through its [GAP-11: REVIEW resplendent] manifestation of divine truth.

---

**¶4**

The third seeking power is Divine Wisdom in its radiance, which came forth from the Infinite, which draws forth all interior wisdom and spiritual life; and it [GAP-12] raises them to elevated states of heaven. Its drawing influence is its own wisdom — [GAP-13: REVIEW the] luminous divine truth by which it draws the souls of people, catching them within that influence. The pervading state of falsity is the general error that dominates spiritual existence, the ruling principle of evil [GAP-14] — the souls that are submerged in that falsity [GAP-15]. It draws them by its influence. They are the souls [GAP-16] whom it draws by its luminous divine truth.

---

**¶5**

The fourth seeking power is the great Divine Providence that [GAP-17] — the living purpose that operates within the sphere of [GAP-18] the whole of spiritual existence at this present day. Yet at the last, in the final judgment and dissolution of all created states, this very living Providence will gather itself inward and form its essential spiritual life into the Ultimate Embodiment. Its drawing influence is its Living Proceeding — for by its proceeding life it can draw forth the wisdom and the spiritual life that is latent in all things, and build these upon its own form. Its containing doctrine, in which it is established, is the accommodated and veiled truth by which it itself moves through the five fundamental spiritual substances [GAP-19] — the great purifying divine love that will consume all the constructed systems of falsity [GAP-20] — what is held within its drawing influence is the wisdom and the spiritual life. It can rescue and liberate these from all the compulsions and bondages of evil and falsity.

---

**¶8**

The first seeking power of the infernal realm is the Ruling Self-Love of those who belong to spiritual darkness, which drew after the living soul by its influence at the beginning of the ages of the world. Its drawing influence is its burning self-love and its cupidity that it has imposed upon the living soul, by which it has entangled the soul [GAP-21], through all the powers at its command.

---

**¶9**

[GAP-22: REVIEW The] second seeking power of the infernal realm is the evil prudence that dwells within [GAP-23] — that draws after the wisdom [GAP-24] and [GAP-25] upward from [GAP-26] the lower states toward the heavenly. It binds them with its powers, which carry them toward the celestial states above. Its drawing influence is [GAP-27] — whereby they are drawn up from the abyss toward the heights.

*Note on ¶9:* This passage resists straightforward translation. Its spiritual sense appears to describe an infernal intelligence that mimics the genuine ascent of truth — a false prudence that intercepts wisdom as it rises from natural states toward spiritual ones, binding it under the guise of elevation. The "drawing upward" here is not genuine liberation but a counterfeit ascent: falsity presenting itself as enlightenment, capturing truths in transit. The paradox of an evil counsel drawing things heavenward corresponds to the spiritual law that the hells can simulate states of heaven in order to ensnare.

---

**¶10**

The third seeking power of the infernal realm is cupidity [GAP-28] — which operates through every faculty of the natural proprium that acts [GAP-29] within the [GAP-30] — drawing the living souls [GAP-31] and enclosing them within its bodily forms, which [GAP-32].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The first hunter is the First Man who was sent from the greatness. He threw himself down to the five storehouses of darkness, he caught and siezed the enmity [of the darkness. And] his net also [he spread it] out over all the children of darkness [... ...]. His ship is his four sons who are swathed over his body. The sea is the land of darkness [... ...]; his net is [his soul] and his powers.

The second hunter is the Third Ambassador. This one, for by his light image, which he revealed to the depths below, he hunted after the entire light that is in all things; as it is established in them. His net is his light image, [that filled] the whole universe and took it prisoner, to this likeness [of the light. His] ship is his light ship. [The sea] is the universe [and all in it] which were hunted after by his net [through] his [glorious] image.

The third hunter is Jesus the Splendour, who came from the greatness, who hunts after the light and life; and he [raises] it to the heights. His net is his wisdom, [the] light wisdom with which he hunts the souls, catching them in the net. The sea is the error of the universe, the law of sin [and death], the souls that are drowning in it [are the fish]. He catches them in his net. They are the souls [that he brings from among th]em by his light wisdom.

The fourth hunter is the great counsel that [is of life] that lives in the circuit [of the] entire universe in it today. Yet, at the end, in the dissolution of the universe, this very counsel of life will gather itself in and sculpt its soul in the Last Statue. Its net is its Living Spirit, because with its Spirit it can hunt after the light and the life that is in all things; and build it upon its body. Its ship, in which it is established, is this light cloud whereby it itself travels in the five elements [Its sea is], the great fire that will burn all the buildings of [the universe. That which is] in its net is the light and the life. It can rescue and free it from all bonds and fetters.

The first hunter is the King of they who belong to the darkness, who hunted after the living soul with his net at the beginning of the worlds. His net is his fire and his lust that he has put upon the living soul, with which he has entangled it [in bonds], through all his powers.

[The] second hunter is the evil counsel that lives in [the world] that hunts after the light [and the life] and [draws them] up from [within] the earths to heaven. It binds them with its powers, which bring them to the heavenly worlds above. Its net is [its cunning] whereby they are drawn up from the abyss [to the heig]hts.
The third hunter is lust [that] walks in every power of the flesh that walks [abroad] in the [world] the living souls [it captures and encloses] them in its bodies, which [... ...].

fills.explanation: The enmity requires a genitive complement identifying whose opposition was seized — only "the darkness" is available in context — and a conjunction is grammatically necessary to transition from the completed action to the new clause beginning "his net also."

A net being verbed "out over" something is strongly constrained to "spread" or "cast"; "spread" matches the spiritual reading's "extended over" and is the standard action for a net in hunting metaphor.

The First Man's net is his interior essence offered against darkness — in Manichaean teaching his soul and his powers together constitute the weapon he deployed; this parallels the progression of net-instruments across the four hunters (soul → image → wisdom → spirit).

The light image pervaded the whole universe (spiritual reading: "pervading the whole field"), and "filled" is the natural Kephalaia verb for a divine image that extends into and occupies the entirety of creation.

The likeness to which the universe was conformed is the likeness "of the light" — the divine light-pattern of the Third Ambassador — completing the clause before the next sentence begins with "His ship."
The editor's choice perfectly matches the systematic pattern where each hunter's description identifies "the sea" as the domain of operation, confirmed across all four divine hunter sections.

The plural "which were hunted after" requires a plural antecedent; "the universe and all in it" provides the necessary plural referent and matches the spiritual reading's "the whole of spiritual existence — all that was drawn."

The spiritual reading specifies "through its resplendent manifestation," indicating the net operates by means of the glorious image; since the net IS the light image, "through" describes how the net's influence is concretely realized.
The editor's "glorious" corresponds precisely to the spiritual reading's "resplendent" and is a standard Kephalaia epithet for the Third Ambassador's manifest divine image.

The spiritual reading states "raises them to elevated states of heaven," and "raises it to the heights" is the natural Kephalaia expression for Jesus the Splendour's action of elevating recovered light and life.
The definite article "the" naturally introduces the appositional expansion "the light wisdom" specifying what kind of wisdom constitutes the net, confirmed by the spiritual reading.

"The law of sin and death" is a fixed formula (cf. Romans 8:2) widely attested in both Manichaean and early Christian texts, matching the spiritual reading's "ruling principle of evil" which encompasses both sin and its ultimate consequence.

The hunting/fishing metaphor requires explicit identification of the quarry: the sea = error, the net = wisdom, and therefore the souls drowning in the sea = the fish, completing the correspondential chain before "He catches them in his net."

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "whom it draws by its luminous divine truth"; Jesus draws/brings specific souls from among those drowning in error, and "th" + "em" forms "them," referring to the mass of souls in the sea of falsity.

The counsel is later explicitly called "this very counsel of life," so the first relative clause identifies its essential nature as belonging to life, before the second clause ("that lives in the circuit") describes its active operation.

"The circuit of the entire universe" is a standard Manichaean cosmological phrase describing the sphere of divine operation, matching the spiritual reading's "within the sphere of the whole of spiritual existence."

Every hunter's description follows the pattern net–ship–sea; the ship clause has just concluded, so this gap must introduce the sea element for the fourth hunter, which is identified as the eschatological fire.

The fire burns "the buildings of the universe" (the constructed systems of falsity), then a new sentence identifies what the net holds: "That which is in its net is the light and the life," matching the spiritual reading's "what is held within its drawing influence."

The spiritual reading describes entanglement of the soul through cupidity; "in bonds" is the natural Kephalaia term for the result of entanglement and directly parallels "bonds and fetters" used in ¶5 of the same chapter.
The definite article "The" correctly opens the paragraph identifying the second infernal hunter, following the same formulaic pattern as every other hunter paragraph in the chapter.

The evil counsel is the infernal counterpart of the divine counsel that lives in "the circuit of the entire universe"; the evil prudence correspondingly dwells within "the world" as the domain where it intercepts ascending truth.
"The light and the life" is a fixed doublet throughout the Kephalaia (cf. ¶4 and ¶5 of this chapter), denoting the twin objects of both divine and infernal hunting.
The evil counsel "draws them up from the earths to heaven" — "draws" is the hunting verb matching the spiritual reading's description of a counterfeit ascent that mimics genuine elevation.

The light and life are drawn "up from within the earths" — trapped within the material earths, they are pulled upward by the evil counsel's counterfeit ascent, matching the spiritual reading's "from the lower states."

The evil counsel's net is its cunning — the instrument of false prudence that simulates genuine spiritual ascent; this is the infernal counterpart to the divine hunters' instruments (soul, image, wisdom, spirit) and fits the spiritual reading's description of deceptive interception.
The relative pronoun "that" connects "lust" to "walks," forming the standard Kephalaia relative clause construction: "lust that walks in every power of the flesh."

The flesh "walks abroad" in the world describes cupidity's pervasive operation through the natural proprium, matching the spiritual reading's "acts within" and using standard Kephalaia vocabulary for widespread activity.

The flesh walks abroad "in the world" — the domain where cupidity operates through the natural proprium, matching the spiritual reading's "within the [domain]" and providing the natural-plane setting for the third infernal hunter.

The spiritual reading specifies "drawing the living souls and enclosing them within its bodily forms"; the medium gap contains the twin actions of lust upon the souls — capturing (drawing) and enclosing (imprisoning) — leading to "them in its bodies."
